_meta.purpose: A SHARED PUBLIC FILTER. Which diseases in GenCC belong to which system of the radar. `src/tools/fetch_gencc.py` reads it and writes `gencc_gene_disease.json`: a gene enters a system when any of its GenCC submissions names a disease that matches the system's filter. This file holds no genes — the genes come from the base, with their classification, mode of inheritance, submitter and date; this file only says what the base is asked for.
_meta.who_writes_this: Whoever composes a system's panel, and they name the source the terms were taken from: a PanelApp panel, a report, a clinical guideline. A system whose entry is empty has not been composed, and the tool leaves it out of the output rather than writing a system with zero genes — «no list» and «a list with no genes» are different states and must stay different on the screen. Since 13.09.2026, by the owner's decision, the BASE composition of every system is written here without waiting for a clinician's signature: a clinically established disease group is composed from the base and the primary analysis runs; what a clinician signs is the curated layer of positions and phrases in system_gene_panels.json, and the exclusions.
_meta.keys: Top-level keys of `systems` are exactly the eleven radar domains that carry a genetic half — the entries of knowledge/radar_domains.json with `genetic_half: true`. The twelfth domain, fitness, is built from wearables and has no genetic half, so it is not a key here. A key that is not a radar domain is a system nothing on the screen can show.
_meta.schema: systems: { <radar key>: { terms: [substring, ...], exclude?: [substring, ...], mondo_ids: [MONDO:nnn or OMIM:nnn, ...], source: '<where the terms came from>' | null, why_empty?: {en, ru} } }
_meta.matching: Terms are matched as case-insensitive substrings against GenCC's harmonised disease title and the submitter's original title. `mondo_ids` are matched exactly against the disease curie — the way to catch a syndrome named after a person, which no substring over its name will find. A filter with terms must carry a `source`; the tool refuses one that does not. `exclude` are substrings that veto a row whichever term it matched — `cystinuria` sits inside `homocystinuria`, `gout` inside `Aicardi-Goutieres`, and no positive term separates them.

thyroid.source: reports/173-evidence-sources-for-system-panels.md (12.09.2026): the names of the two Genomics England PanelApp panels it cites — «Congenital hypothyroidism» (panel 31) and «Hyperthyroidism» (panel 236) — and the disease names it lists from GenCC for the seven genes of the thyroid panel a clinician sent: thyroid dyshormonogenesis, hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, abnormal thyroid hormone metabolism, resistance to thyroid hormone, athyreosis, thyroid hypoplasia, thyroid cancer. «thyroid cancer» is kept although the one row it matched there was Limited: the loader keeps every classification and the engine decides what prints. PanelApp's own gene lists are NOT copied — its licence for redistribution is unverified — only the panel names are used as terms.
thyroid.not_terms: Dysgenesis without «thyroid» beside it, «goiter» and «thyroiditis» were not added: they are not in the report, and a term is added from a named source, not from what would seem reasonable.
